purpose: T0.10: does vectorising Grackle help? Its production build has -O3 but ZERO -march/-x flags.

config.note: IDENTICAL Enzo binary (c73ee4b6) in both arms - libgrackle resolves via LD_LIBRARY_PATH, so only the library differs. Verified: enzo.exe has no RPATH/RUNPATH, and ldd resolves to the AVX2 library with the prepend and the production one without.

build.location: foggie_bench_root/grackle-avx2 (out-of-source; production build at /u/jtumlins/grackle/... left untouched, verified by unchanged CMakeCache md5 and .so mtimes)
build.flags: GRACKLE_OPTIMIZATION_FLIST=-march=core-avx2, all other options matched to production (Release, double, OpenMP off, shared, same compilers, same HDF5)
build.instruction_level_proof: production .so: 0 %ymm, 0 FMA, 0 vector ops. AVX2 .so: 386 %ymm, 453 FMA, 1568 vector ops.

verdict: NULL RESULT. Wall -1.0%, ChemistryCooling -1.8% - both inside the noise floor. Vectorising the chemistry kernels does essentially nothing.
why: Surprising given the instruction counts, and worth recording so nobody repeats it: Grackle's chemistry solve is an implicit ODE integration with per-cell sub-cycling and convergence tests. Iteration counts are data-dependent, so neighbouring cells exit at different times and the SIMD lanes cannot stay in lockstep. The kernel is branch- and latency-bound, not arithmetic-bound; vectorisation only helps the latter.
recommendation: Close T0.10 as a negative. Do NOT rebuild production Grackle expecting the audit's 1.5-3x - that figure was for scalar hydro kernels on Pleiades, and does not transfer to an implicit chemistry solver. If chemistry is ever revisited, the lever is algorithmic (fewer sub-cycles / looser tolerance / gating the solve), not the ISA.
caveat: One sample per arm. Effect sizes are small enough that repeats would only narrow 'nothing' to 'nothing', but no repeat was run.
